blindSummary:
This country has the region's second-strongest record of pro-LGBT judicial protection, behind one regional peer. Its high court decriminalised same-sex conduct in a 2019 judgment upheld on appeal in 2021; the court of appeal ordered the government to register a national LGBT organisation; and trans people have won document-change cases, the first in 2017. Draft 2024 constitutional changes even contemplate intersex rights. Implementation lags the rulings (an international litigation centre documents unsatisfactory compliance), social conservatism persists, and there is no general legal-gender-recognition statute — but the courts are a genuine protection, unique in the region.

For a visitor: decriminalised, functioning courts, moderate social hostility.
blindOutOfScope: Legal-gender recognition requires per-case litigation; implementation gaps are resident-facing.
blindSourceSummaries: International litigation centre article (May 2024) by two human-rights lawyers: courts in this country and a neighbouring country have issued landmark LGBTQI+ rulings (here: registration of a national LGBT organisation ordered in 2016; a 2019 high-court decriminalisation upheld on appeal in 2021), but implementation of the orders has been unsatisfactory - governments slow to comply.
Risk-advisory firm (June 2024): this country's proposed constitutional change would protect intersex rights - analysis of the reform process.

UN UPR outcome report for this country (43rd session, May 2023): recommendations to repeal a penal-code provision criminalising same-sex conduct for women and to introduce a clear administrative process for legal gender recognition did not enjoy this country's support; same-sex relations between women remain criminalised and no administrative process for legal gender recognition exists.

A foreign government's 2011 human-rights report on this country: general human-rights assessment (violence against women, prison conditions, discrimination against marginalised indigenous communities) - the LGBT section documents the then-criminalised status and societal discrimination.

National LGBT organisation's official blog: the organisation's activities - World AIDS Day commemorations, HIV stigma work, participation in a regional LGBTI network's conference - documenting the community organisation's operations after winning its registration battle.

Foreign daily (Dec 2017): this country's High Court ordered the government to legally recognise a trans woman's gender for the first time - the director of a trans-rights organisation will receive a female ID card after a four-year legal battle; a landmark for trans rights here.

NOTE: page content did not load at fetch time (only an international human-rights organisation's site navigation was retrieved); the underlying Jan 2018 piece argues 2018 will be 'the year of courts' for LGBT rights, citing this country among the litigation fronts.
blindLocalsOnly: Document-change rights exist only via per-case litigation (the first won in 2017); there is no general legal-gender-recognition statute — resident-facing; implementation gaps documented by an international litigation centre.
blindTangential: The 2019 decriminalisation removed same-sex-conduct exposure for visitors travelling with partners.
